なかま食堂.name: Nakama Shokudo
なかま食堂.desc: A local diner along Route 58 in Nakama, Onna Village. Its signature is the soki soba (¥1,200), served with a huge spare rib on a separate plate that looks like part of a BBQ set. The round, udon-like straight noodles and the pork-bone-forward blended broth are distinctive too, making for a very photogenic bowl.
t: This article was created with AI (Chat GPT 4o) and partly supplemented by me 😁

I ate here in November 2024 😄 This time I visited “Nakama Shokudo” in Nakama, Onna Village. It is a nostalgic-feeling local diner, easy to spot by its orange noren (shop curtain) and the banners fluttering in the wind.
Nakama Shokudo
And waiting here was an Okinawa soba that sticks in your memory for its sheer visual impact.
Menu
Menu
My order that day was the “soki soba (¥1,200).” The moment I saw the tray being brought over, I couldn’t help but say “Wow!” 😅
Soki soba　¥1,200

Served on a separate plate from the soba was, believe it or not, a gigantic spare rib. It’s the size of something from a BBQ set, and it hardly looks like a “soki” at all. It grabs you with its impact before you’ve even taken a bite.

Now, let me start with the broth. It looks clear, but when I took a sip it had a mysteriously unusual flavor. I think it’s probably based on a blended broth, but the pork-bone flavor came through rather strongly. Even so, I felt it had a character a bit different from the broth of typical Okinawa soba.
Soki soba　¥1,200

And then the noodles. These surprised me a little. They weren’t the kind of noodles you often see in Okinawa soba — they were round, straight noodles! They look just like udon. The texture is on the soft side. It’s quite a rare type for Okinawa soba, and for a moment you almost get the illusion of “Wait, am I eating udon today?” (lol) But it has a strange charm that makes you think “this works too.”

The star of the show, the spare rib, is simply packed with volume without any complaint 💥 It’s seasoned well with a sweet sauce and simmered until falling apart. It’s so tender the meat slips right off the bone, the flavor soaks in thoroughly, and the meat alone is satisfying enough.
Inside the shop
There’s vinegar among the condiments 😆

The shop has a homey atmosphere, and it’s easy to see why there are so many tourists. Looking at the menu, there are plenty of soba set meals and side dishes too, so it seems like an easy diner to use for a daytime drink or with the family.

The taste is more “just plain tasty” than “superb!” Still, I’d like you to experience the combination of this spare rib’s looks with the distinctive noodles and broth at least once. It was a photogenic bowl that I think would go over well with tourists 📷
Rating (9/15): It’s just plain tasty. If you want to experience a “giant spare rib,” I definitely recommend the soki soba at Nakama Shokudo 🍜✨

畑すば.name: Haru Suba
畑すば.desc: A lone-house-in-the-middle-of-nowhere Okinawa soba shop in Yamada, Onna Village, down a forest road leading from Route 58 toward the Yamada Castle ruins (the name is read “Haru Suba”). A homey place with a pork-bone-forward broth, medium-thick straight noodles, and sweetly seasoned bone-in pork ribs that leave an impression.
t: I ate here in April 2024 😁
Haru Suba (On Route 58 in Yamada, Onna Village, there is a sign like the one in the photo on what looks like a narrow forest road, and if you enter from that road you end up here 😁)
Haru Suba
Haru Suba (It’s a shop with real character 😁)

Whenever I drove along Route 58, I always wondered about this shop, because there is a sign on what looks like a forest road leading to the “Yamada Castle ruins” in Onna Village (I’ve never been there (^0^;)), so this time I went to check it out 😆
Once you enter the forest road, it is relatively close.
Menu
The menu is small. It’s a homey kind of place 😄 I decided to order the “soki soba.”
Soki soba　¥800
I took a sip of the broth 😁 It has a pork-bone-forward broth. It’s ordinary 😆
Soki soba　¥800
Next, the noodles. They are medium-thick, straight, and on the soft side. The bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) were also tender, and the sweet seasoning left an impression.

Rating (9/15): It’s ordinary. Although it’s close to the highway, it is where the road goes up into the hills, so it’s a lone-house-in-the-middle-of-nowhere kind of shop 😁 It’s in Onna Village, a tourist destination, so why not drop by once when you come to Onna Village?

そば処 一本松.name: Soba-dokoro Ipponmatsu
そば処 一本松.desc: A local diner tucked away in a residential area of Toyama, Urasoe City. By far the most popular dish is the “Stamina Soba,” a three-way platter of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki). Its clear broth of pork bone, kelp, and bonito with a soft waft of garlic is a distinctive feature.
t: * This article was created based on AI (Chat GPT 5 Thinking) and partly supplemented by me 😁

This time I ate here in January 2025 😆 After circling around the residential area of Toyama, Urasoe City, I finally found “Soba-dokoro Ipponmatsu.” With its pure white exterior wall and the stately carved wooden sign, it looked so tasteful that I couldn’t help taking a photo 📸
Soba-dokoro Ipponmatsu

Next to it is a bright red vending machine, and potted plants at its feet add a little seasonal color. The atmosphere of a local diner is already drifting out from the entrance. Since it’s a bit off the main road, it’s easy to get lost on a first visit, but seeing the neighborhood people entering one after another the moment it opened, I thought “this is surely a winner” and my expectations rose steadily 😊
Inside the shop
Inside, the wooden tables and chairs are neatly polished, and along the wall are self-service water and tea, pickled red ginger, and condiments.
Menu

Opening the menu, there are rows of photos on yellow paper. The shop’s top recommendation, the “Stamina Soba” at ¥1,100, is prominently featured, and the “Ipponmatsu Soba,” which bears the shop’s name, is ¥750 for small and ¥850 for large, kids’ soba is ¥400, and yushi-dofu soba and yushi-dofu soup are ¥800 each. Rice is ¥100, jushi is ¥200, iced coffee is ¥200, and a medium bottle of beer is ¥550, so the prices are balanced in a way that is friendly to both tourists and locals 💴 Of course this time I ordered the by-far most popular No. 1, the “Stamina Soba.”
Stamina soba　¥1,100

The moment the black bowl arrived on a wooden tray, along with the steam came the soft scent of garlic layered over a blended broth of pork bone, kelp, and bonito flakes. First a sip... the broth feels clear in the mouth, and the outline of the bonito steps smoothly to the front 🐟
Stamina soba　¥1,100
The noodles are medium-thick with a gentle wave, boiled on the soft side so they slide down easily 🍜

The toppings are a stamina trio worthy of the name. The star, the meat, comes as a three-kind platter, occupying half the bowl with hefty, chunky presence. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is well seasoned with a rather strong sinewy texture. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are melt-in-your-mouth and light, so soft that even the bouncy collagen becomes one with the meat, and I was impressed by how cleanly the fat breaks. The bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) have the fat trimmed for an elegant finish, though they too have a strong sinewy bounce 🥢 Partway through I sprinkled on the free fuchiba (mugwort) 🌿

My overall impression is “a satisfying soba that stays close to everyday life.” Locals gather right from opening time, and it’s nice that the shop’s secluded location deep in the residential area keeps a calm atmosphere 🏡
Rating (9/15): However, in terms of the flavor of Okinawa soba, it ends up settling at “just plain tasty” after all 😌 Why not try this shop at least once? 😆

我如古そば.name: Ganeko Soba
我如古そば.desc: A traditional diner in Gusukuma, Urasoe City. Its signature is the Ganeko soba, with a gentle, translucent pork-bone broth and thick, wavy noodles. There is also a free fried chicken service on Saturdays and a free jushi service on the 14th of every month. A popular local spot with a full lineup of set meals.
t: * This article was created by AI (Claude Opus 4.5) with some additions and updates by me 😆 I ate here in February 2025 😄

This time I visited “Ganeko Soba” in Gusukuma, Urasoe City! Looking at the exterior, the words “Ganeko Soba” on the wooden sign are striking. A pink noren hangs at the entrance, giving off the feel of an old-fashioned Okinawa soba shop 🏠
Ganeko Soba

Inside, the two-tone orange and blue walls stand out, and it has a nostalgic diner style. A few table seats are lined up, and handwritten menu items like “tebichi nitsuke (braised pig’s feet),” “nakami soba,” and “tebichi soba” are posted on the walls ✨
Inside the shop
Menu
Menu
Menu

Looking at the menu, it’s not just Okinawa soba but a full lineup of set meals too. There is “braised pig’s feet set meal” ¥1,200, “soki soup” ¥1,200, “nakami soup” ¥890, “liver and vegetable set” ¥930, “ginger pork set” ¥950, “vegetable champuru” ¥850, “katsudon” ¥880, “champon” ¥880, and more — an abundant lineup typical of an Okinawan diner 🍽️

The Okinawa soba menu also offers plenty of variety: “soba set meal” ¥930, “Okinawa soba” ¥700, “sanmai-niku soba” ¥750, “soki soba” ¥800, “tebichi soba” ¥980, “nakami soba” ¥890, “mugwort soba” ¥800, “squid-ink soba” ¥800, and so on. Kids’ soba at ¥400 is also a nice point for families 👨‍👩‍👧

And I found a bargain campaign too! Every Saturday is “Fried Chicken Day,” with 2 pieces of fried chicken free with a soba order 🎉 Also, the 14th of every month is “Jushi Day,” with one bowl of jushi free with a soba order. You can apparently swap it for white rice if you like. Today happened to be the 14th, so I got the jushi as a free service! Lucky 😆
This time I ordered the “Ganeko Soba” (¥820), which shares its name with the shop. After a short wait, it was brought out together with the jushi 🍜
Ganeko soba　¥820 (* jushi free on the 14th)

In the bowl is a translucent pork-bone broth with thick, slightly wavy noodles. The toppings are two slices of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), fish cake (kamaboko), and green onions. It looks satisfying just by appearance 😋
First, a sip of the broth. It has the gentle flavor of pork-bone stock. It has no off-notes and is a comforting taste. The saltiness is just right, and it’s an easy-drinking broth.
Ganeko soba　¥820
Next, the noodles. They are thick, wavy noodles with a soft texture. A simple flavor typical of Okinawa soba 🍜

The braised pork belly and bone-in pork ribs toppings are both lightly seasoned. The braised pork belly has a decent balance of fat and lean, but has a bit of a sinewy texture. The bone-in pork ribs are the same: the seasoning is gentle, but there were parts where the sinew remained.
I also had the complimentary jushi. This too is lightly seasoned, like a simple Okinawan seasoned rice. Eating it together with the soba fills you right up 🍚

Looking around the shop, many local customers were coming in and it was lively. Many were ordering set meals, and I felt this is a shop beloved by the locals. It’s very ordinary Okinawa soba, but that “ordinary” is exactly what’s good about it 😊

Rating (9/15): It was a very ordinary, tasty Okinawa soba. It has no special distinguishing character, but it’s a reassuring bowl that makes you understand why the locals love it. With such a full set-meal lineup, you’ll want to try things other than Okinawa soba too. If you come to Urasoe City, why not drop by? 😊
